clue.text: Put to death, one died, canonised apparently?

blocks.note: a canonised person is a saint, abbreviated St and placed before the name
taken as written
D is the standard abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A martyr is executed and later declared a saint, like Stephen.
explanation.walkthrough: Canonising someone gives them the title of saint, which is written before the name, so that piece leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoning was a method of execution, so someone killed this way was put to death by thrown rocks.

clue.text: Flags prepared, raised round Ireland

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards
going round something means wrapping it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: set means ready or prepared
IR is the international abbreviation for Ireland

explanation.surface: Banners are got ready and hoisted around Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags' looks like a noun for banners, but it is the verb meaning weakens.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to grow weary or lose energy, which is what someone does who tires.

clue.text: Novel on top state

blocks.note: novel as an adjective means new
a jersey is a top, a knitted garment for the upper body

explanation.surface: A book sits on top of the pile, or a fresh shirt is worn.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty United States, on the Atlantic coast between New York and Pennsylvania.

clue.text: Figure like playground chaser

blocks.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
in the game of tag the child doing the chasing is called it

explanation.surface: A shape that resembles a child running after others at school break.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a single numeral from nought to nine, written as a figure.

clue.text: Reportedly, sovereign power knocked for six

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound counts and not the spelling

blocks.note: the throne stands for the power of a monarch

explanation.surface: A king's rule is said to be overturned completely.
explanation.walkthrough: To knock someone for six, from cricket where the ball is hit out of the ground, is to stun or upset them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrown means being disconcerted or confused, just as a person knocked for six is badly shaken.

clue.text: Score also picked up for mark in rugby

indicators.note: picking something up by ear means hearing it, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a score is twenty
too means also

explanation.surface: A tally of points is also heard about in a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: On a rugby pitch the 22-metre line, called the twenty-two, is marked out in front of each try line.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenty-two is the line painted twenty-two metres from each try line on a rugby field.

clue.text: Clean water in several houses

blocks.note: first meaning: to wash something lightly
second meaning: the water used in homes everywhere to wash out soap or dirt

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a loose description of the water used for this job in many households.
explanation.definitionFit: A rinse is a quick wash in plain water, and to rinse is to clean by flushing with water.

clue.text: Wide lane, it is mistaken for middle

indicators.note: something mistaken is wrong, so these letters are in the wrong order and must be put right

blocks.note: W is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a wide
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A broad road is confused with the central one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wide' reads as an adjective for the lane, but it supplies one letter to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The waistline runs round the narrow part of the body, so it is one's middle.

clue.text: Obtuse angle below centre of boat

indicators.note: the centre is the middle, so only the inside letters of that word are kept

blocks.note: the two middle letters of boat
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A wide geometric angle sits underneath the middle of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obtuse angle' looks like geometry; 'Obtuse' alone is the definition, meaning dim. In a down clue 'below' puts the second piece underneath the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse can mean slow-witted or stupid, and an oaf is a clumsy, dull person.

clue.text: Corny as Lancashire, perhaps?

blocks.note: first meaning: trite and sentimental
second meaning: like a Lancashire, an English crumbly cheese, so tasting of cheese

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lancashire' seems to be the county, but here it is the cheese named after it; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Corny jokes are clichéd and sentimental, which slang calls cheesy; the word also simply means like cheese.

clue.text: Sign a concern, briefly pointing the wrong way

indicators.note: something put briefly is cut short, so the final letter of the word goes
facing the wrong way means the shortened word runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a worry is a concern

explanation.surface: A signpost points the wrong way, which is briefly worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortening happens first and the turning round second, and only the shortened word is turned.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a sign showing direction, the kind painted on roads or printed on signposts.

clue.text: Inexperienced magician with no time for London Town

indicators.note: having none of something means it is taken away from the word before

blocks.note: green means new to something, untried
a witch works magic
T is the abbreviation for time; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A novice conjurer can't find time for the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magician' is not the whole definition of anything; it names a spell-caster whose name loses one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenwich is a district of south-east London, once a separate riverside town, home of the meridian.

clue.text: Look at Pakistan’s opener in cricket, for example?

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so only the initial letter of the country is kept
one piece sits inside the other word

blocks.note: a cricket is one kind of insect
first letter of Pakistan

explanation.surface: Watch Pakistan's opening batsman in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' and 'cricket' together suggest an opening batsman; the cricket is the chirping insect. P goes inside INSECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, a more careful way to look at something.

clue.text: Passion in Turner oddly shows

definitions.note: a collective noun for staged performances, standing for the plural

indicators.note: read oddly, only the first, third, fifth letters and so on of the painter's name are kept
the first word goes inside the selected letters

blocks.note: the odd-placed letters of Turner
heat means intensity of feeling, passion

explanation.surface: The painter Turner's work shows strong feeling in places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shows' looks like the verb, but it is a noun: staged performances.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre is drama as a whole, the plays and performances staged for an audience.

clue.text: Leaders cutting advantage

blocks.note: heads are leaders, as of departments or schools
a cutting remark is sharp or tart

explanation.surface: Bosses reduce their lead over rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' seems to be a verb acting on the advantage, but it is an adjective meaning sharp-tongued.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is an early lead given or gained at the beginning, which puts someone ahead of rivals.

clue.text: Disbelief at fitting in puzzle pieces

indicators.note: the word is fitted around the others, so they sit inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a maze is a puzzle of paths
the pieces in chess or draughts are called men

explanation.surface: Someone can't believe how the jigsaw pieces fit together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle pieces' suggests a jigsaw; the two words supply separate pieces, which go inside AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazement is great surprise, the feeling of scarcely being able to credit what one sees.

clue.text: In temporary accommodation I have to be considerate

blocks.note: at can mean in, as in at home
a tent is a temporary shelter
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A camper says they must be thoughtful while living under canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: An attentive person is thoughtful and mindful of others' needs, which is what considerate means.

clue.text: Just imaginary, ultimately, mythological being

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of that word is kept

blocks.note: just means fair, even-handed
last letter of imaginary

explanation.surface: A legendary creature turns out to be merely made up in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'only', but it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy is a small magical creature of folklore and legend with supernatural powers.

clue.text: Aficionado hosting fashionable banker

indicators.note: a host takes a guest in, so the first word holds the second inside it

blocks.note: a fancier is an enthusiast, as in pigeon fancier
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: An enthusiast throws a party for a stylish banker.
explanation.walkthrough: A fancier is someone keen on breeding or keeping something, like a pigeon fancier.
explanation.definitionFit: A financier manages large sums of money and investments, as a banker does.

clue.text: Money at one’s fingertips

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for cash, often as the readies
second meaning: immediately available, to hand

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as cash being within easy reach; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready is old British slang for available cash, and ready also describes anything prepared and close to hand.

clue.text: Stuffing of roadie knocked out, set for sleep

indicators.note: the stuffing is what fills the inside, the part about to be removed
the filling is knocked out, so only the outside letters of that word remain

blocks.note: outer letters of roadie once the middle is gone
to pose a question is to set it

explanation.surface: A roadie is knocked unconscious and laid out to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: A roadie is a member of a band's touring crew. 'Knocked out' suggests unconsciousness, but it removes the middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is rest or sleep, the state of lying still and relaxed.

clue.text: Most troublesome, riots then breaking out

indicators.note: something breaking out bursts apart, so these letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The worst trouble comes when riots erupt.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny problem is prickly and difficult, so the thorniest is the most awkward and troubling.

clue.text: Canopy in street, fabricated

indicators.note: something fabricated is made up or built, so these letters are constructed into a new word

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An awning is put up along a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester is the cloth canopy over a four-poster bed, an old word for that overhead covering.

clue.text: Wine drunk by little man before daylight

indicators.note: a drink taken by someone goes inside them, so the second word holds the first

blocks.note: a pawn is the smallest chess man
red is red wine

explanation.surface: A small fellow drinks wine before the sun comes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little man' suggests a short person, but it is the humblest piece in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Predawn describes the dark hours just ahead of sunrise, the time before daylight.

clue.text: Exhausted, no one going out then?

blocks.note: first meaning: completely worn out
second meaning, read literally: if nobody leaves, everyone stays indoors

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is a playful literal reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: All in is informal for utterly tired, too worn out to carry on.

clue.text: Bendy food round the bend

blocks.note: first meaning: the curved yellow fruit, in the plural
second meaning: mad, crazy

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves play on bending: the fruit is curved, and round the bend is British slang for insane.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas are curved fruit, and going bananas is slang for losing one's mind, which is what round the bend means.

clue.text: Fitting offer on film

blocks.note: a bid is an offer, as at auction
ET is the Spielberg film about an alien

explanation.surface: A suitable offer is made for a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' looks like an adjective meaning suitable; it is a noun for a fixture. In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidet is a low basin plumbed into a bathroom, one of its fixtures or fittings.

clue.text: Jog is good to take part in altogether

indicators.note: taking part in something means joining it, so one letter goes inside the other word

blocks.note: in the altogether is a jokey phrase for naked
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Going for a run is a good way to join in, all together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jog' suggests running, but it is the verb meaning to push gently.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone is to give them a small push, which is what a nudge is.

clue.text: Restriction after period of time for entrance

indicators.note: coming after means the first-named piece is placed second, behind the time period

blocks.note: a spell is a stretch of time
a bind is a constraint or restriction

explanation.surface: Limits are imposed on how long people may come in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' reads as a way in, but it is the verb, stressed on the second syllable, meaning to enchant.
explanation.definitionFit: To spellbind someone is to hold them captivated, just as to entrance them is to fill them with wonder.

clue.text: Pass by popular music genre

blocks.note: in means popular, fashionable
to pass away is to die

explanation.surface: Walking past a style of pop music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass by' reads as one verb, but the words split: one for each piece, with 'by' putting them side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Indie is guitar-based alternative rock, named for the independent labels that first released it.

clue.text: Scent a catastrophic position taken

indicators.note: a catastrophe throws everything into disorder, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A smell signals that someone has adopted a disastrous attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is an attitude or standpoint one adopts on an issue, or a way of standing.

clue.text: Cad knocked over, achieve objective

indicators.note: a thing knocked over ends up upside down, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a rat is a scoundrel, a cad
to get something is to achieve or obtain it

explanation.surface: A bounder is felled, and the aim is accomplished.
explanation.walkthrough: A cad is an old-fashioned British word for a man who behaves dishonourably.
explanation.definitionFit: A target is an aim or goal one is working towards, an objective.
